Business justification: A portfolio-aligned operator name reduces onboarding friction for Platform Operators deploying new products and supports a coherent product identity as the portfolio grows. It also eliminates the need to create and maintain a separate operator for RHAIIS on OpenShift, reducing net new development work and ongoing support burden. This is strategically important as the Red Hat AI portfolio expands beyond OpenShift-specific tooling.
User problem: Platform Operators see an operator named 'Red Hat OpenShift AI' which implies it is specific to OpenShift, creating confusion as the portfolio expands to cover broader AI products like RHAIIS with distributed inference across xKS and OpenShift. The current naming also blocks the natural reuse of this operator for new products without creating a misleading product identity.
Scope: Single focused need — a renaming effort across all customer-facing artifacts (CRDs, API groups, container images, namespace defaults, CLI references, metrics, traces, telemetry, documentation). No functional changes to operator behavior, capabilities, or supported configurations. Must include seamless upgrade path from RHOAI to RHAI without redeploying managed workloads or manual CR migration.
Success criteria: All customer-facing operator artifacts carry the new RHAI name with no remnants of RHOAI naming; existing RHOAI installations can upgrade to RHAI without redeploying managed workloads; existing Custom Resources created under RHOAI continue to reconcile after upgrade without manual migration; metrics, distributed traces, and telemetry reflect the new naming convention; Platform Operators can confirm rename completion and operator health from existing monitoring; installation guide, upgrade guide, and CRD reference documentation updated to reflect the new name with explicit transition steps.", "priority": "Blocker", "prompt": "We need to rename the Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) Operator to Red Hat AI (RHAI) Operator. The current name is too narrow — it implies the operator is specific to OpenShift, but we're expanding the portfolio to include things like Red Hat AI Inference Server (RHAIIS) with distributed inference on both xKS and OpenShift. Rather than building a completely new operator for RHAIIS on OpenShift, we want to leverage the existing RHOAI operator, but the name needs to reflect the broader portfolio scope.
